title: What the live paper record shows
description: The engines' own state, read from the running record: what is open, what closed, and what the market filter is doing right now.
body:
Paper signals only. No real orders are placed anywhere in this record. One trade says nothing about a strategy. The live records for these engines start on different dates: v005 counts its live record from 1 October 2026 and v006 from 9 October 2026. The first live signal was an ATOM entry at 2.066 after the 10 October 2026 daily close. ATOM exited below its 10-day low at the 18 October 2026 close, at 1.703, which is -17.9% after the 30 bps round trip. A NEAR entry at 5.896 on 12 October 2026 has been open since. In testing, the average winner was roughly +19%, so a losing start is the expected case rather than a surprise. The same numbers appear on the performance page, in the signal log, and in the status posted to the channel.

## Open positions and the market filter

At the snapshot read at 2026-11-11T20:58:06.145Z:

- htf-rsi-v007 shows 0 positions open on paper.
- trend-daily-v005 shows 0 positions open on paper, and its Bitcoin market filter is off.
- trend-daily-v006 shows 0 positions open on paper, and its Bitcoin market filter is off.
- Separately, a NEAR entry at 5.896 on 12 October 2026 has been open since.

The engine-level counts and the NEAR position are both part of the live paper record, and they are reported without reconciling one into the other. With both trend-daily engines showing the Bitcoin market filter off and 0 open paper positions, the record shows no paper trend exposure being held by those engines at that snapshot. The market filter state and the open-position count are separate fields in the engines' own state. Both are reported as they are, and neither is converted into a market-direction claim.

## Closed trades

- htf-rsi-v007 has 4 closed trades so far, with an average null net per trade.
- trend-daily-v005 has 6 closed trades so far, with an average -13.22% net per trade.
- trend-daily-v006 has 7 closed trades so far, with an average -13.34% net per trade.

The ATOM trade is the most recent closed trade described in detail: it entered at 2.066 after the 10 October 2026 daily close and exited below its 10-day low at the 18 October 2026 close at 1.703, for -17.9% after the 30 bps round trip. These averages summarize completed paper trades over short live records that began on 1 October 2026 for v005 and 9 October 2026 for v006. They are not forecasts and do not imply that the next trade will resemble them. The ATOM result is one completed paper trade in a record where a losing start is the expected case, because testing showed an average winner of roughly +19%.

## Distance to the 20-day breakout

For both trend-daily engines, the symbols closest to their 20-day breakout are the same three:

- TRXUSDT is 9.82% below its high.
- BNBUSDT is 10.43% below its high.
- UNIUSDT is 12.53% below its high.

A 20-day breakout entry depends on a new high, so a symbol that is below its high by 9.82%, 10.43%, or 12.53% has not met that condition at the measured time. The record therefore shows no trend-daily paper entry from this breakout rule among those symbols at the snapshot. These percentages measure distance from a recent high; they do not predict whether the symbol will later reach a new high. Because the same three symbols and the same three percentages appear for both v005 and v006, the two engines are observing the same market distance at this snapshot.

## What the record can and cannot show

The record is paper only. It contains no real orders, no live capital, and no claim that any pattern will repeat. The closed-trade averages, the open NEAR position at 5.896, and the ATOM loss of -17.9% describe what has happened in a short live record. The testing expectation that the average winner was roughly +19% is a historical testing statement, not a promise about these live paper trades. A single trade says nothing about a strategy, and a short record says little about long-run behavior. The snapshot was read at 2026-11-11T20:58:06.145Z, and the record updates continuously.

## Where to check the numbers

The same numbers appear on the performance page, in the signal log, and in the status posted to the channel. That includes the engine states, the closed-trade counts and averages, the filter states, the breakout distances, and the snapshot timestamp. Because the record updates continuously, a later check can show different open positions, different closed-trade counts, or a different filter state. This article is a snapshot taken at 2026-11-11T20:58:06.145Z.
